title: Learn a codebase by redesigning it with an agent tutor
summary: A developer made a Claude Code skill where an agent maps a project's key design choices from its code and history, then quizzes you to work them out yourself.
agent_role: A background agent reads the code, file links and commit history to build a list of 5 to 10 design problems. The tutor agent asks guiding questions, narrows choices when you are stuck, and logs where you struggled. The learner does the reasoning.
what_they_did: Eric Zou built a skill called rederive. You type /rederive in your coding agent and point it at a project, like the Express web library. It asks why the project exists and how you'd solve the problem. Meanwhile a background agent maps 5 to 10 design problems in build order. It only asks questions and never just explains.
worth_knowing: The map file holds the answers, so don't open it until you finish. The agent ignores commit messages, so it works even on projects built in a few big commits.
prompt: Help me understand the codebase at [repo path or URL] by having me redesign it myself. First, quietly study the code, how files connect, and the commits where the design changed. Write 5 to 10 key design problems in the order they'd be built to a notes file I won't read. Then start by asking me what problem the project solves. Guide me through each design problem with questions only; don't explain the answer. If I'm stuck, narrow it to a few options. After two wrong answers, offer a sketch. At the end, summarize where I struggled.

curation.rationale: An original learning use: a background agent maps a repo's design history while a tutor agent quizzes you. Code and a sample session exist, but no reported learning results.
